name: Kimi Brand Tokens
description: Kimi (Moonshot AI) brand design tokens. Hex values, font families and official URLs are sourced from the official Kimi Brand Guidelines. Token role names and the derived spacing/grid scale are a working assignment by this skill, not verbatim official naming.

deepBlue.role: 深蓝 — 品牌蓝轴的高对比端，小字号正文、深色强调、渐变暗端

azure.role: 亮蓝 — 渐变端点、次级强调、数据系列

sky.role: 天蓝 — 浅底背景、色块、辅助填充

electricCyan.role: 电光青 — 深色场景高亮、图表焦点

lavender.role: 淡紫 — 生成式视觉、柔和分区

blush.role: 淡粉 — 暖色分区、人文温度场景

mint.role: 薄荷绿 — 成功态、生长隐喻

citron.role: 淡黄 — 提示态、探索隐喻

ink.role: 墨黑 — 深色底、正文文字

slate.role: 深灰 — 次级文字、图标

graphite.role: 中灰 — 禁用态、图表中性底

white.role: 白 — 浅色底、反白文字

derived.$comment: Not part of the official 15-color palette. Observed on kimi.com for dark-mode hairlines and raised surfaces; included so dark mode has a defined elevation ramp without inventing new hues.

inkBorder.role: 深色底分隔线与描边（官方页面实际使用值）

contrast.$comment: WCAG 2.1 measured ratios, verified with the standard relative-luminance formula. These record where colour stays legible. They are NOT a reason to substitute brand colours — official values are used as published.
contrast.slate-on-mistVerdict: below AA — slate is a pure-white-surface text colour only; on the mist section/zebra/alt-canvas it drops below 4.5
contrast.inkOnBrandBlueVerdict: AA at any size — the safe default pairing for a brand-blue fill
contrast.brandBlue-on-white-verdict: meets the 3:1 large-text threshold only; below 4.5, so it is not compliant for normal-size text and is not used for body links
contrast.brandBlueOnWhiteUse: fills, non-text UI, graphics, and text at large sizes only (>=24px, or >=18.66px at 700)
contrast.white-on-brandBlue-verdict: same as brandBlue-on-white — large text only (>=24px, or >=18.66px at 700)
contrast.silver-on-white-verdict: decorative only on light surfaces — never carries text there
contrast.silver-on-inkVerdict: AAA — this is the correct secondary text colour on dark surfaces
contrast.slate-on-dark-verdict: too weak for axis or label text on dark surfaces; use silver
contrast.electricCyanVerdict: dark-surface focus colour only — invisible on white, so light charts must focus with deep blue
contrast.accentOnInk: 12.2-16.9 for all four accent colors — AAA on dark
rules: Do not substitute official brand colour values to chase a contrast number.
Pick the text colour for the background it will actually sit on: a colour that passes on white can fail on the mist section fill.
Light-surface body links use deep blue #002F5B (13.48:1). Brand blue #007CFF is 3.94:1 on white and is used for fills, non-text UI and large-text emphasis.
On a brand-blue fill, use ink #121212 (4.75:1) for text at any size.
White on a brand-blue fill is only compliant at large-text sizes: 24px, or 18.66px at weight 700.
Slate #707070 is secondary text on pure white only; on mist #E1E3E6 it is 3.85:1, so use ink there.
silver (#C3C3C3) carries text on dark surfaces (10.63:1) but never on light ones (1.76:1).
Electric cyan (#00F6FF) is a dark-surface accent only; it is 1.34:1 on white.

sans.role: 正文、UI 文本、表格、导航、按钮、表单

mono.role: 代码、命令行、终端、指标数值、版本号

serif.role: 引文、标语、大字标题性表达

grid.base: 标准化基础网格 — 4/8 步进间距，跨端一致，用于表格、表单、密集正文、后台界面
grid.expressive: 多元表现力网格 — 仅用于文字少、视觉主导的场景（大图、封面、Hero、品牌影片帧）

dataViz.nonTextNote: WCAG 1.4.11 — a chart series that is the only cue for its value needs 3:1 against the canvas. Measured against BOTH the primary and the alt canvas of each theme.

lightSeries.note: Only these four of the 15 official colours clear 3:1 on white AND on the mist alt-canvas. On a light canvas the number is set by contrast, not taste.

lightSeriesRejected.#8D9390: 3.13 on white but 2.43 on mist — usable on a plain white canvas only

dataViz.lowContrastEscapeHatch: A fill below 3:1 may still be used for a large area (where the shape is not the only cue) or when paired with a 1-2px outline in a colour that does clear 3:1. The outline becomes the discriminating edge.

darkSeries.note: 12 of the 15 official colours clear 3:1 on ink AND on the raised surface, so contrast alone does not cap the count. Five is a design recommendation: among those 12, several sit within about 1.2:1 of each other in luminance on ink (for example #A0DAF7 vs #DFC8F5 at 0.13 apart, #B3F4A8 vs #E1E3E6 at 0.08), so a larger set cannot be told apart reliably. Pick series that stay distinguishable rather than merely visible.

darkSeriesRejected.#002F5B: 1.39 on ink / 1.01 on raised — invisible on dark
darkSeriesRejected.#121212: 1.40 on the raised surface — the canvas itself

dataViz.focusNote: Deep blue, not electric cyan: cyan is only 1.34:1 on a white surface. Axis labels are ink, not slate: slate is 3.85:1 on the mist alt-canvas.
dataViz.sequentialRampNote: A sequential ramp is an exception to the 3:1 series rule: it is read as a gradient, not as discrete series, and each step is labelled. The light end still needs a visible boundary against the canvas.
dataViz.darkFocusNote: Cyan is safe on ink (13.94:1) and is the correct dark-surface focus colour. Axis labels must be #C3C3C3: #707070 would be 3.78:1 on ink and only 2.71:1 on the raised surface.
principles: Minimalism and reduction; the chart must first and foremost accurately convey the data.

A series that is the only cue for its value must clear 3:1 against its canvas (WCAG 1.4.11). On a light canvas that leaves 4 colours; on a dark canvas contrast leaves 12, and the recommended 5 is about telling series apart, not about visibility.
Never truncate or distort an axis in a way that misleads.
No 3D charts, no dual Y axes, no pie charts with more than 5 slices.
Numeric labels use Geist Mono with tabular-nums.
